response.internal_assessment: Module 1 is done. That is a real fact. But I need to be honest with myself about the other two: I do not have confirmation that I submitted an application or canceled a subscription last tick. The outcome note says 'you opened the SQL course and completed Module 1' — and that is all it says. That silence is data. It means I did the thing that felt like learning and growth and forward motion, and I probably deferred the two things that felt like commitment and risk and finality. That is exactly what status_quo_bias looks like when it's working on you — it doesn't stop you from doing everything, it lets you do the comfortable thing and stops you short of the uncomfortable thing, and then it says: you did something, that's enough. The policies are at 26. Angela is talking to a lawyer. Maria Santos named a timeline. My runway is 6 months. 'Module 1 is enough' is a sentence I am not allowed to believe right now.

chosen_actions.description: Complete Module 2 of the SQL course tonight. Not schedule it, not read the overview — open it and finish it. Module 1 was the proof I could start. Module 2 is the proof that last tick was a habit forming, not a one-time event.
chosen_actions.reasoning: The status_quo_bias move after completing Module 1 is to feel good about it, slow down, and treat 'started' as a destination. Module 2 tonight is the direct counter to that. Two months is 60 days. If I complete one module every two days I will have meaningful SQL skills in 6 weeks, which is inside the deployment window. If I let two or three days slip between modules, I will have moderate SQL skills in 4 months, which is after. The math on urgency and pace is not abstract.

If I did do it last tick and I'm being too hard on myself, then doing it again this tick is still the right answer: I need a pipeline of applications, not a single one. One application is a lottery ticket. Three applications is a search. The first rejection will make the second application easier to send. I need to start that sequence now, not after I finish the SQL course.

chosen_actions.description: Look up Maria Santos's $2,500 retraining grant application process. Determine eligibility. If the application takes under an hour, complete and submit it tonight. More importantly: applying for this grant is a public act. It is me telling a government program that I am a worker who is transitioning out of an automating sector. That is a true statement. Saying it out loud — even on a form — is the kind of irreversibility I committed to last tick and did not fully execute. I am exactly the person this grant was designed for. Not applying because I haven't gotten around to it would be absurd.
